newsitem.title: USA: ECC holder starts proxy, recommends co sale.
newsitem.headline: ECC holder starts proxy, recommends co sale.

text.p: An ECC International Corp shareholder said on Wednesday he started a proxy contest, and recommended ECC hire an investment bank to sell the company or its businesses.

Shareholder Michael Taglich said: "Wall Street analysts believe ECC's defense business segment alone could be worth $13 to $15 per shares, and the vending business could be worth an additional $2 to $3."

Taglich, president of New York brokerage firm Taglich Brothers, D'Amedeo, Wagner & Co Inc said he proposed by-law changes to allow shareholders owning 10 percent or more of the company's shares to call a special meeting at any time.
The company was not immediately available for comment.
Taglich criticized the company's recent bylaw changes as insincere because they could be changed by the board at any time and did not require shareholder approval.
ECC had also set an unreasonable 30 percent threshold for calling a special meeting, Taglich said.

"The company has stated in its proxy that its opposition to the engagement of an investment banker is founded on the belief that uncertainty as to the future control and direction of the company would have a negative impact on potential new contracts," Taglich said. "I do not share this concern." He said management and shareholders had different agendas.
